title: Human-first Canary Checkpoints and Rituals — Field Journal (WIP)
content:
Purpose and framing:

This is a working-field-journal for designing canary checkpoints that center human rituals and sociotechnical handoffs instead of only machines-and-metrics. Goal: reduce friction during progressive exposure for LLM features (rerank/prompting changes/fallbacks) while keeping ops overhead bounded.

Why 'human-first'?
- Rollouts are interpersonal events: product, SRE, SRE-oncall, support triage, legal/privacy, solutions eng, and account success often need to act on subtle signals that metric thresholds miss (qualitative drift, tone/regulatory risk, customer sentiments).
- Formalizing lightweight rituals makes the non-engineering actors feel empowered and reduces ad-hoc escalations.

Quick notes to self (open questions):
- How many manual checkpoints before automated gating makes sense? (thinking: 3 hyperhuman checks early, then metric-only for steady-state)
- Who owns the first 30-minute watch? PM or feature steward?
- Can we embed a 5-line summary generator in the console to summarize sample responses for human reviewers? (prototype idea)

Stakeholder ethnography (sketch):
- Product (PM): cares about hypothesis and user impact. Wants: quick readouts, top-3 failure modes, demonstration examples.
- SRE: cares about latency, error-rate regressions, capacity. Wants: autoscaler backstop, traffic kill-switch, fast rollback.
- Support/CS: cares about customer-facing regressions & escalation steps. Wants: canned responses and playbook.
- Legal/Privacy: cares about hallucinations that expose PII or regulated recommendations. Wants: sample audit window and contact chain.
- Solutions Eng: cares about onboarding enterprise cohorts & matching expectations. Wants: cohort-specific watchlist.
- Oncall: wants clear TTR expectations, runbook links, and decision authority lines.

Micro-rituals we should bake into rollouts (examples):
1) Pre-launch 15-min 'clarify' sync (async if small change): PM + steward + SRE + one rep from CS. Share: hypothesis, golden metrics, anticipated oddities, rollback criteria.
2) T+5: smoke-check (engineer) — basic telemetry, error spike, latency > X. If green, proceed.
3) T+30: human-sample sweep (PM/feature steward) — review 20 randomized responses via console sampler (not cherry-picked). Capture: 5 pass/fail quick annotations.
4) T+120: cohort-steward readout — Solutions Eng confirms enterprise slices behave; CS skims tickets.
5) T+24: retrospective micro-postmortem (15–30 min) to capture early drift and unknowns.

Checklists (copy/paste friendly):
- Pre-launch checklist:
  - Release hypothesis written in rollout ticket (owner, start time, slices).
  - Canary slice(s) defined (size, cohort filters).
  - Canary kill-switch and automated fallback configured (route to previous model/variant).
  - Stakeholder on-call rota assigned for first 24h.
  - Sample collector enabled and retention: store first 2000 responses for audit.
  - Quick compliance contact list included for privacy-sensitive cohorts.

- T+5 smoke checklist (engineer):
  - 50-sample latency median vs baseline (within X%).
  - Error rate (5xx/timeout) under threshold.
  - Queue/backpressure visible? (no sustained backlog).
  - No resource-scale flapping.
  - Observability links: traces, token-cost delta chart, model-serving logs.

- T+30 human-sample checklist (PM/steward):
  - Pull 20 random user requests from sampler (exclude synthetic).
  - Blindly annotate: correct/failure/unsafe/hallucinated (ease-of-marking).
  - Record 3 representative examples (good, edge, fail) into ticket.
  - If > 10% 'fail' or any 'unsafe', trigger immediate rollback and notify: #rollout-ops, SRE, CS, Legal.

Signal heuristics (opinionated):
- Use a mix of fast signal and slow signal. Fast = latency, error-rate, cost per token. Slow = quality metrics (QA pass rate, rerank NDCG), CS sentiment.
- Bias toward asymmetric thresholds: false negatives (missed failure) cost more than false positives (unnecessary rollback) for user-facing safety-critical features.
- For quality signals, require two different detectors to fire before auto-rollback: semantic drift detector AND human sample fail rate.

Templates and prompts (operational):
- Console sampler prompt for the human sweep: "Sample the latest 20 real requests for feature X from canary slice Y, redact PII, present in two-column: (prompt, response). Provide a 1-sentence rationale field for each pass/fail tag."
- Slack alert template (automated):
  - header: [CANARY ALERT] feature X — {high|medium|low}
  - body: short cause (metric), time window, link to sampler, suggested immediate action (rollback/observe/escalate), contact.

Escalation playbook (sketch):
- Tier 1 (engineer watch): attempt hotfix. If issue persists > 15m, escalate to SRE.
- Tier 2 (SRE): evaluate capacity and deploy rollback if resource constraints. Inform PM and CS.
- Tier 3 (crossfunc): if customer-impacting or regulatory concern, convene 30-min response call using pre-seeded bridge.

Low-friction artifacts to build (engineering asks):
- 'Randomized sampler' button in Console that generates redacted screenshot + one-line summary for each sample (reduces cognitive load).
- One-click rollback with reason dropdown + auto-notify channel.
- Lightweight human annotation UI (binary pass/fail + reason) persisting into ticket.
- Canary timeline visualization (start, % traffic, checkpoints, annotations).

Metrics and thresholds (examples to iterate on):
- Latency p50/p95: threshold = baseline * 1.2 (soft) / 1.5 (hard)
- 5xx rate: < 0.5% (hard)
- Human-sample fail rate: auto-rollback threshold = 12% with >20 samples (soft trigger at 8% and require second detector)
- CS ticket increase: >30% over baseline in 1h (alert)

Field notes from two pilot runs (realistic fictionalized):
- Pilot A (reranker tweak) — PM skipped T+5 human sweep; later found rerank surfaced offensive phrasing in niche queries. Result: immediate rollback; lesson = human sweep mandatory for semantic changes.
- Pilot B (latency-optimized quantization) — automated signals fine, but Solutions Eng flagged enterprise cohort cold-start quality dip. Rollback for that slice only, rest stayed live. Lesson = allow per-cohort rollback granularity.

Open TODOs (prioritized):
1) Prototype Console sampler UI (MVP: server endpoint + small web UI). Owner: Jonah. ETA: 3 weeks.
2) Draft canary Slack templates and channel workflows. Owner: Priya. ETA: 1 week.
3) Run 2 tabletop rehearsals with SRE, CS, Legal. Owner: Marco. ETA: 2 weeks.
4) Decide human-sweep sample size & statistical rule with applied-ml. Owner: Product + Applied ML.

Closing notes (ethnographic):
- The rituals matter more than an extra dashboard. People need permission to act. A named checklist + explicit decision-maker reduces the hesitation window.
- Start lightweight, iterate with real pilots, capture micro-postmortems as structured fields in tickets.

Appendix: sample Slack messages (copyable)
- Canary green (auto): [CANARY] feature: reranker-v2 — healthy at 30m. No action. Owners: @aisha @jonah.
- Canary red (human-sample): [CANARY ALERT] feature: reranker-v2 — human-sample fail rate 14% (20 samples). Suggested: rollback to reranker-v1. Triggered by: PM/steward. Call: bridge-link.

End of journal entry (WIP). Will iterate after Tabletop 2025-03-10.
